root_cause.text: In arm64 ptrace's sve_set_common(), commit 9f8bf718f292 wrongly made the TIF_SVE state update conditional on system_supports_sme(), so on SVE-without-SME systems NT_ARM_SVE writes could store FP_STATE_SVE data without setting the tracee's TIF_SVE flag, leaving inconsistent task state.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message explicitly says the bug was introduced when “the setting of TIF_SVE was moved into a block which is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true,” and the patch removes the outer `if (system_supports_sme())` around the `ARM64_VEC_SVE` case that does `set_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE);`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit message explicitly says the bug was introduced when “the setting of TIF_SVE was moved into a block which is only executed when system_supports_sme() is true,” and the patch removes the outer `if (system_supports_sme())` around the `ARM64_VEC_SVE` case that does `set_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE);`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always apply SVE/SME type-specific thread state updates in `sve_set_common()` instead of incorrectly gating them on SME system support.
intent_record.what: The change removes the outer `if (system_supports_sme())` conditional around the `switch (type)` in `sve_set_common()`, leaving the `switch` to always execute for `ARM64_VEC_SVE` and `ARM64_VEC_SME` cases, while keeping the same per-case updates to `target->thread.svcr`, `TIF_SVE`, `TIF_SME`, and the default `WARN_ON_ONCE(1); return -EINVAL;` handling.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now always performs the vector-type-specific state transition logic instead of skipping it when SME is not system-supported. This ensures SVE requests still clear `SVCR_SM_MASK` and set `TIF_SVE`, and SME requests still set `SVCR_SM_MASK` and `TIF_SME`, preventing the function from silently omitting these updates on systems where `system_supports_sme()` is false.

grouping_result.intent: Always apply SVE/SME type-specific thread state updates in `sve_set_common()` instead of incorrectly gating them on SME system support.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the root cause in sve_set_common(): it removes the incorrect dependency on system_supports_sme() and ensures SVE/SME-specific thread state updates, including TIF_SVE handling, are always applied appropriately.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the root cause: it wrongly gates the SVE-specific state update logic on SME system support, so on systems with SVE but without SME the ARM64_VEC_SVE case is skipped and TIF_SVE is not set despite storing SVE state.

This is the required state update for SVE tasks; because it is nested under the incorrect system_supports_sme() condition, it may not execute on SVE-without-SME systems, leaving task state inconsistent.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional incorrectly gates the SVE/SME type-specific state update logic on SME system support. On systems that support SVE but not SME, the ARM64_VEC_SVE handling is skipped, so FP_STATE_SVE data can be stored without updating the task's SVE state flags, causing inconsistent task state.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full relevant logic in `sve_set_common()`, so it is sufficient to judge. The root cause is that updating `TIF_SVE` became conditional on `system_supports_sme()`, allowing NT_ARM_SVE writes on SVE-without-SME systems to populate SVE state without setting the flag. In this function, the only unconditional `TIF_SVE` handling for full SVE writes is later in the path: `fpsimd_sync_to_sve(target);` followed by `set_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE);`, which is correct for the full-register case. However, the new SME-specific mode-switch block is guarded by `if (system_supports_sme()) { ... }`, and inside it the code changes streaming mode and may call `sve_alloc(target)`. The vulnerability described is specifically that this commit made the TIF_SVE state update depend on SME support; this commit is exactly the introduction of `sve_set_common(..., enum vec_type type)` and the new `if (system_supports_sme())` split. There is no compensating fix here that ensures the TIF_SVE state is updated independently of SME capability in all relevant NT_ARM_SVE write cases. Therefore this commit version contains the vulnerable construct and does not yet contain the later fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code is sufficient because it includes the full SVE ptrace setter logic introduced in this commit, including the state-flag updates relevant to the root cause. The vulnerability described is that a later commit made the TIF_SVE update conditional on `system_supports_sme()`, which could skip setting `TIF_SVE` on SVE-only systems. That vulnerable construct is not present here. In this commit's `sve_set()` full-SVE path, after `fpsimd_sync_to_sve(target);` the code unconditionally executes `set_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE);`. Likewise, in the FPSIMD-only case it unconditionally executes `clear_tsk_thread_flag(target, TIF_SVE);`. There is no `system_supports_sme()` check anywhere in this logic, so the specific vulnerable condition does not exist in this function. At the same time, this commit does not contain the later fix for that later regression; rather, it predates the regression entirely. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent (`has_bug=false`), and this version should not be considered to already contain the fix for that later bug (`is_fixed=false`).
